newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says greater investment needed to create jobs.
newsitem.headline: EU says greater investment needed to create jobs.

text.p: Greater investment in the European Union's productive capacity is needed to tackle the mounting rise in joblessness, the European Commission said in a report on Wednesday.

Responding to a call from EU leaders to study the mutually beneficial effects of closer economic policy coordination, the Commission, the EU's executive, said, "The rise in unemployment over the past 20 years has directly reflected the decline in the share of investment in GDP (gross domestic product)."
At present capital investment in the EU accounts for 19 percent of GDP compared with 24 percent during the early part of the 1970s.
Some of the decline in investment could be explained by falling profitability, which in recent years has improved, the report added.

With nearly 18 million out of work in the EU, efforts to create jobs have taken on greater urgency, particularly against the backdrop of tightening budget policies which have often been blamed for slow pace of employment growth.
The Commission's report will go to a summit of EU leaders in Dublin on December 13 and 14 and will include several other areas of importance for future policy.

Among them is the observation that the EU has a massive "under-used labour reserve" and that a major effort is needed to equip workers for the jobs of the future, particularly in the service sector. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
